What is Holafly Plans and is it worth it?

Holafly Plans is a monthly eSIM subscription covering 160+ destinations on a single eSIM. Light is $49.90/month for 25GB; Unlimited is $64.90/month. It's worth it for travelers staying 30+ days or moving between multiple countries, since it consistently undercuts the cost of stacking destination eSIMs and eliminates the admin of buying a new plan at every border.

Can I use one Holafly eSIM in multiple countries?

Regional plans cover multiple countries in one region — the Europe eSIM covers 40+ countries, the Asia regional covers Thailand, Japan, Vietnam, Singapore, and more. For worldwide multi-country travel, the monthly Plans subscription covers 160+ destinations on a single eSIM installation.

Does Holafly include calls and texts? [...] For our Da Nang base we tend to use the Vietnam destination eSIM for long stays. For shorter multi-country trips — say, Bangkok for two weeks then Chiang Mai then Hanoi — the regional plan often wins on price and always wins on convenience.

## When Monthly Plans Make More Sense

For any trip longer than 30 days, or if you're moving countries often enough that buying individual destination eSIMs gets tedious, Holafly's Plans subscription changes the calculation. One eSIM. One monthly price. 160+ destinations. No buying a new plan every time you cross a border.

| Plans Unlimited | $64.90/month | Unlimited global | [...] How much does Holafly cost per day?

Does Holafly work well in Japan?

Yes. We've used Holafly in Japan for 325 days across multiple trips. It runs on NTT Docomo's network and delivers consistent 4G/5G in cities, on Shinkansen bullet trains, in rural areas, and in Tokyo's subway tunnels. It's our most-tested destination and one of the strongest performers.

results.content:
In August 2024, I was on a work trip to four countries in Southeast Asia (Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore) so I bought an Airalo regional eSIM card for Asia that was 10GB of data for 30 days for $37. Again, country-specific eSIMs are a better value. For example, my 30-day Japan eSIM was only $24.15 for 30 days for 20GB, which is a much better value for a lower price than my regional Asia eSIM. [...] ### Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam eSIMs

In early 2025, I traveled to Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam using Airalo using country-specific eSIM cards for each place, but they are all covered on Airalo’s regional Asia eSIM plans. First of all, Airalo is the only eSIM company with coverage in Laos from my research. You can buy a Laos-only eSIM (limited options and pricey—$9.50 for 1 GB), and it’s included in the regional Asia eSIM (better value). [...] When I left Singapore, I flew to Japan for a month-long trip and used up the leftover data on my regional Asia eSIM before switching to a Japan-only eSIM. I spent part of my work trip in Japan on a ship traveling around Japan and knew we were going to Busan, Korea for one day so I bought a 5GB regional Asia eSIM ($18.55 for 30 days) to use there. (They also offer cheaper 7-day plans with less data, but I always need to maximize my data so I usually buy the 30-day ones.)

results.content:
(Credit: Nomad/PCMag)

In the US, Nomad offers six regular plans: 1GB for $4.50 (seven days), 1GB for $6 (seven days), 3GB for $11 (30 days), 5GB for $14 (30 days), 10GB for $24 (30 days), and 20GB for $35 (30 days). Though they offer the same 1GB of data, the $4.50 and $6.00 plans are indeed different. The $4.50 plan supports AT&T and T-Mobile and starts automatically when connected to a network or after a 30-day window. The $6.00 plan is limited to just AT&T but provides a more flexible 60-day activation window.

Nomad also offers shorter day plans ranging from 1 to 10 days that come with 1GB of high-speed data per day plus unlimited data throttled to 512Kbps. The website and app clearly outline each plan’s details, and all listed prices include applicable taxes.

(Credit: Nomad/PCMag) [...] (Credit: Nomad/PCMag)

Nomad's US pricing is in line with other data-only service providers like Airalo and Saily, which charge $4.50 and $4.39, respectively, for 1GB of data over 7 days.

To use Nomad's eSIM service, your device needs to be unlocked and eSIM compatible. Many modern phones, such as the Apple iPhone 16 and the Samsung Galaxy S24, support eSIMs. If you are unsure if your device will work with Nomad, the company lists the phones, tablets, and laptops that are compatible with its service. [...] (Credit: Iyaz Akhtar)

You can view your data usage in the Manage tab of the Nomad app, where you can also see details like when your plan will expire and buy more data. If your data is running low or is set to expire, you will receive a notification. You can purchase additional data at the same price as regular plans. For example, an additional 1GB costs $4.50.

## Data plans and pricing

Customers ordering an eSIM have to choose how much data they need and how long they need it for. Saily is flexible on both counts, offering multiple data plans for most destinations.

For example, let's say you are visiting Malaysia. Prices vary depending on your chosen plan, starting at $1.99 per week to $35.99 monthly (with a 20 GB limit) in Czechia, Bulgaria, and Mayotte. [...] Saily also offers regional plans that cross borders. For instance, the European plan covers 36 countries (a much cheaper option than purchasing eSIMs for multiple countries). There are also regional plans for Asia and Oceania (19 countries), Africa (34 countries), Latin America (12 countries), North America (Canada and the USA), and the Middle East and North Africa (19 countries).

The global plan is also worth noting. It's not technically "global" as data plans only cover 113 countries (as of April 2025). Even so, the global plan ranges from Antigua to Iceland. It's a great value option for those with complex travel plans, especially for the year-long plan. [...] Device owners order digital SIMs via the Saily app. Saily then links their device to local network providers wherever they are. Whether you are vacationing in Barbados or traveling in Japan for business, Saily offers immediate internet coverage, often at much lower prices than standard SIMs or eSIM rivals.

Users can also use the Saily ad blocker and web protection, which help limit tracking and reduce the risk of slowdowns or unwanted access. You can also change virtual locations.

## Saily eSIM card: How it works

As you probably know, smartphones and tablets use a physical SIM card to access network coverage. The SIM card (or "Subscriber Identity Module") holds the user's phone number and identification data to make calls or surf the web.

Luckily, it’s worth the extra. Holafly’s coverage means no roaming charges in any state. Plus, it relies on AT&T networks to provide 4G LTE and 5G connections. 为你的亚洲之旅选择合适的 eSIM 能让你在保持联网的同时节省开支。由于亚洲地域辽阔，地形多样，通信基础设施各不相同，因此选择一款覆盖可靠、符合你旅行需求的 eSIM 至关重要。以下是在挑选亚洲最佳 eSIM 时需要考虑的因素：

Luckily all of the main companies have booths at Taoyuan airport, so you’ll be able to compare prices at a glance. After you’ve cleared immigration and collected your bags, walk out into the arrivals hall and turn right. Follow the signs for the buses — just before you get to the end of the arrival hall and escalators to take you down to where the buses leave from, you’ll see several booths on your right.

You can get an unlimited 7 day data plan with Chunghwa for 450 NTD (around $13.50 USD). Check what the other companies are offering as well, but that’s not a bad deal. If you don’t need that much data, 1GB costs 180 NTD, and 2.2GB costs 300 NTD, valid for two months.

Overall I do believe that the value derived from a Sim Local plan is higher than that of other eSIM providers that I’ve used in the past. [...] You’re supposed to be able to check your usage by dialing #123#, but for some reason that wasn’t working for me. I could have reached out to them on WhatsApp to get clarification while on my trip, but I never got around to it, so it wasn’t too big of a deal to me.

Alternatively, I just looked at my cellular settings on my phone to see how much data I had used, so this was a good enough checkpoint for me.

## How does Sim Local compare to other eSIM providers?

The Sim Local Asia regional plan that I used offered 20GB of data along with 50 SMS and 15 minutes of calling for $35 USD.

For a comparable data package size, Ubigi offers a 25GB data plan for 30 days in Asia for $44 USD. This is more expensive compared to Sim Local and does not come with SMS and voice. [...] They offered a package that completely fit my needs at a very affordable price ($35 USD compared to the $204 it would otherwise cost me with my domestic carrier’s travel plan). The connection and the overall experience was smooth and seamless, I ran into very few issues with the service itself, and it felt like I was using my phone just like I was back at home.

I’ll definitely be using it on my next international trip coming this summer!

Once-off prices for eSIMs in South Africa range from $4.50 to $26 and include between 1 GB and 10 GB of data. Depending on your plan, that's just $2.60 to $4.50 per gigabyte, which isn't bad for a country like South Africa. Most travellers should be able to get by with these amounts without any problems. Setting up and activating your eSIM happens entirely on your smartphone, and it's very quick. In our test, we just took two minutes (watch our how-to video on YouTube to see how it's done). Moreover, you can easily top this up via the Airalo app if you start running low on data during your trip. This saves you time and hassle compared to buying a physical SIM, where you'd usually need to stand in line at the counter to buy or top up your card or package. [...] Going back to eSIMs, Yesim's packages cost between $15.40 and $55 in South Africa for 3 GB to 20 GB (that's just $2.75 to $5.13 per gigabyte), with contract durations lasting from seven to 30 days. Yesim also offers three unlimited packages in South Africa for seven- and fifteen-day durations, although the upfront cost is higher at $31.90 and $51.70, respectively.

It's worth remembering that, depending on your plan, Yesim's prices can sometimes be fractionally lower per gigabyte than Airalo's, so if you're looking for the best deal, make sure you visit Yesim's website and compare their prices to Airalo's directly.

Visit Yesim's website now

## How Do They Compare? [...] Like its larger competitors, Yesim gives you an eSIM card connecting to local carriers while you're in South Africa (specifically MTN and Vodafone networks). It can be installed quickly and effortlessly right from the app or via a QR code sent to your email after purchase. Interestingly, alongside its eSIM service, Yesim also offers a virtual number service that allows you to get an online-only US (+1), Canadian (+1), or Israeli (+972) mobile phone number to use for apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram, OpenAI, Binance, Tinder, or TikTok. These virtual numbers can be used for a flat fee of $2.75 per month.

## 4. Regional eSIM Price Comparison

 Europe: 5GB ($5–$15) | 10GB ($10–$25) — excellent multi-country bundles, lowest average cost due to roaming agreements.
 Asia: 5GB ($3–$20) — Southeast Asia offers the world's cheapest data; Japan and Korea are mid-to-high tier with premium networks.

## 5. Provider-by-Provider Price Comparison [...] ## 6. Cheapest eSIM Plans by Use Case

 Short trips (1–7 days): 1–3GB ($3–$8) → navigation, messaging, ride-hailing.
 Europe travel (multi-country): 5–10GB ($5–$15) → regional bundles provide best cross-border value.
 Long stay (15–30 days): 10–20GB ($15–$30) → optimal cost per GB for remote work or extended vacation.
 Heavy data users / streaming: unlimited or 20GB+ ($25–$50+) → stability and hotspot support for work and entertainment.

## 7. How to Compare eSIM Prices Correctly [...] eSIM plans typically cost $2 to $50, depending on destination, data size, and validity period.  
The cheapest options are small regional plans (1–3GB), while global or unlimited plans cost more due to broader coverage and flexibility.

You can get an unlimited 7 day data plan with Chunghwa for 450 NTD (around $13.50 USD). Check what the other companies are offering as well, but that’s not a bad deal. If you don’t need that much data, 1GB costs 180 NTD, and 2.2GB costs 300 NTD, valid for two months.

That’s the option I’ve suggested to friends who’ve visited Taiwan in the last couple of years, and they’ve all come back happy with the speeds, service, and (especially) cost.

I’ve found aloSIM to typically have the lowest prices, usually around ten bucks for 10GB of data, with smaller and larger options available. If you don’t need much data, take a look at Instabridge as well: its smaller bundles can be very cheap.
